text:
Christian Dvorak scored the winner against Buffalo on Tuesday, a two-point night that got him player of the game, and it was a reminder of what Philadelphia asks of him. He plays nearly 18 minutes a night, often against the other team's best (Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 97th percentile last season), and has 4 goals and 14 points in 25 games.

The scoring is honest. His goals sit right at his expected goals (the quality of his chances), and he's been steady lately, with points in seven of his last ten games. The worry is five on five. The Flyers get only about 41% of the expected goals with him on the ice, more than four points worse than when he sits, and they're out-attempted too. Some of that is the matchups. Not all of it.

He's a quick skater, top fifth of the league in bursts over 20 mph, with a soft shot, so his goals come from position rather than release. Last season he put up 51 points, the best year of his career. We'd watch whether the even-strength results improve, because a matchup center lives or dies by them.
